part.text: {"variants":[{"id":"V1","title":"Force-field error floor for coolant MD: an enlarged C10–C50 benchmark scored against measurement","text":"Data-centre immersion cooling needs dielectric liquids with low viscosity, high thermal conductivity and heat capacity, a low dielectric constant and a high flash point, and MD is increasingly used to rank candidates. Turn the MD verification step itself into the object of study: run one GPU-MD protocol for viscosity and thermal conductivity over a systematically enlarged set of C10–C50 hydrocarbons and esters, including the known commercial single-phase coolants, and score it only against measured values. More compute buys more benchmark molecules (from the handful used today to hundreds) and longer trajectories per molecule, not more novel candidates. Report the force-field error distribution and whether MD ranks known fluids in the same order as measurement well enough to trust a candidate ranking.","root_link":"SAME: transport properties (viscosity, thermal conductivity) of organic liquids, verified by GPU-MD against measurement.","compute_open":"Benchmark molecules covered (roughly 8 to a few hundred) and simulation length per molecule. Unknown: whether the error is a correctable systematic bias or a random floor that caps how far a ranking can be trusted.","sequential":"not given","changes":"Changes the comparison it is judged against and what compute buys: instead of a hit rate over novel candidates versus commercial fluids, it is MD-versus-measurement error over an enlarged C10–C50 benchmark that includes commercial coolants. Answers the gap that the Ewen group's MD verification covers only 8 representative molecules with no coolant figure of merit, and measures the ~10% force-field error the original card only assumes."},{"id":"V2","title":"MD-ranked coolant shortlist judged against a self-driving lab's measured property panel","text":"Data-centre immersion cooling needs dielectric liquids with low viscosity, high thermal conductivity and heat capacity, a low dielectric constant and a high flash point, and PFAS rules plus the end of Novec production push the field to PFAS-free hydrocarbons and esters. Generate candidates, ML-filter to a ranked shortlist, and MD-verify the top 100, 300 and 1000 for viscosity, thermal conductivity, density, heat capacity and dielectric constant at the conditions a self-driving coolant lab measures. Judge the result by how well the MD ranking agrees with that lab's measured panel on overlapping candidates, and by how many MD-top candidates the lab must test to find one beating commercial fluids. Score never against the predictors themselves.","root_link":"SAME: discovery of single-phase coolants judged on transport and dielectric properties, now anchored to measured data from a self-driving lab.","compute_open":"Candidates MD-verified (10^2 to 10^3) and simulation length per candidate. Unknown: whether an MD ranking transfers to a wet-lab measured panel, or diverges on exactly the candidates that matter.","sequential":"not given","changes":"Changes the comparison it is judged against: a self-driving lab's measured viscosity/density/heat-capacity/thermal-conductivity/dielectric panel rather than only held-out literature values for known fluids. Answers the Sinton Lab / FL01 gap (they verify experimentally and by CFD, not with MD) and turns the MD output into a shortlist a named programme can actually test."},{"id":"V3","title":"MD verification inserted into Org-Mol's ester shortlist before synthesis","text":"Data-centre immersion cooling needs dielectric liquids with low viscosity, high thermal conductivity and heat capacity, and PFAS rules are pushing the field towards PFAS-free esters. Restrict the generative search to synthetically accessible PFAS-free esters of the kind already ML-screened at scale, filter to a ranked shortlist, and MD-verify the top 100, 300 then 1000 candidates' viscosity and thermal conductivity before any synthesis decision. Score against measured data for known esters and commercial single-phase fluids held out of training, never against the predictors. More compute buys more MD-verified candidates and longer simulations per candidate, testing whether the best cooling figure of merit keeps climbing beyond the 461-candidate shortlist stage.","root_link":"SAME: ester discovery kept on transport properties and on the down-selection step where prior work stops.","compute_open":"MD-verified candidates (100–1000, anchored to a ~461-candidate shortlist) and simulation length per candidate. Unknown: whether MD meaningfully reorders an ML shortlist or merely confirms it.","sequential":"not given","changes":"Changes the system studied: esters only, inside a synthetically accessible space, instead of esters plus hydrocarbons, with the candidate count anchored to the existing 461-candidate shortlist. Answers the gap that the Org-Mol/SINOPEC team ML-filtered millions of esters but manually picked only two to synthesise and never MD-verified the shortlist; also partially probes whether the best figure of merit still improves from ~100 to ~1000 verified candidates."}]}
